# France: under the rule of a contested politico-administrative elite whose legitimacy erodes

Edward Elgar Publishing eBooks. Published: 2022-10-18. Book chapter. 1 citation.

## Abstract

France, a country of high administrative tradition (where the word "bureaucracy" was even invented in the 18th Century), represents a very interesting case, under its current regime - the Fifth Republic after 60 years of evolution -, of a rather unique combination of classic 'functional politicization' of the higher public administration (in Mayntz and Derlien sense) with a very French "administrafication of high level politics". In the latter phenomenon the existence of huge and powerful ministerial (and presidential) cabinets of politically appointed special advisors belonging to the higher civil service by profession yet politicians by destination, is a major factor. Contemporary France, especially under President Macron, is thus governed-an-administered by a rather integrated State elite, whose legitimization by hyper-selection through grandes écoles and technocratic competence used to be strong but is more and more contested in the public, while the democratic legitimization of the whole system of power comes mainly/only from the direct election by universal suffrage of Presidents who quickly become unpopular and face difficulties to run successfully for reelection.
